title: Islais Creek’s replacement project closed while its temporary bypass needed extending

beats.text: San Francisco built a temporary sewer bypass while it planned a permanent replacement.

visual.sub: The emergency repair had a separate budget

beats.text: In 2019, the permanent crossing was scheduled for 2023.

visual.kicker: The emergency repair had a separate budget

beats.text: The temporary bypass was substantially complete in October 2019.

visual.kicker: The emergency repair had a separate budget

beats.text: Three years later, the permanent design was on hold.

visual.kicker: The permanent design went on hold

beats.text: The replacement project had already spent more than ten million dollars.

visual.label: The permanent design went on hold

beats.text: The Controller’s vouchers identify two separate engineering contracts.

visual.kicker: Two contract numbers identify separate engineering payments

beats.text: The crossing project closed in June 2025.

visual.kicker: A narrower project closed below its revised budget

beats.text: It recorded nearly twelve million dollars in expenditures.

visual.label: A narrower project closed below its revised budget

beats.text: The recorded scope now described surveys and inspections.
Another project took on the bypass life extension.

visual.kicker: A second project carried the cost of extending the bypass

beats.text: Its estimated completion slipped by 427 days.

visual.label: A second project carried the cost of extending the bypass

beats.text: The utility cited added bypass work and higher underwater repair costs.
The utility later estimated seventeen million dollars for the bypass extension alone.

visual.label: A second project carried the cost of extending the bypass

beats.text: That was a procurement estimate. Final construction payments remain an open question.

visual.kicker: A second project carried the cost of extending the bypass
